questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: In 1923, Weimar Germany suffered HYPERINFLATION. What does that mean?
options: Money lost value so fast that prices exploded daily
The banks ran out of coins
Wages were frozen for a decade
questions.answer: Money lost value so fast that prices exploded daily
questions.why: Prices doubled in days — people carted wages in wheelbarrows. It shredded trust in the young Weimar Republic, and that lost trust matters later in your unit.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Area of a parallelogram: base 8 cm, height 5 cm?
questions.why: Parallelogram = base × height, NO half. 20 is the trap — halving belongs to triangles only.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Lord of the Flies: which boy is mocked for his weight and glasses — but does the clearest thinking?
questions.why: Piggy — the island's brain, treated as its joke. Watch how the boys use his ideas while refusing him respect. That gap IS one of Golding's points.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Weimar Republic was Germany's first real attempt at…
questions.why: Born from WWI defeat in 1919 — Germany's first democracy, and it carried the blame for Versailles from day one.

questions.subject: Geography
options: A growing share of people living in cities
questions.answer: A growing share of people living in cities
questions.why: Urbanisation = the city share growing. Migration = people MOVING (between places or countries). Related, not the same — a classic exam trap.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.prompt: A MARKET ANALYSIS in a business plan mainly examines…
questions.why: Who will buy, and who else is selling to them — the two questions every market analysis must answer.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.why: Triangle-area arithmetic: 10 × 9 = 90, halve it → 45. You know this cold — last question, no rush, take the extra second.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: How did the Great Depression help the Nazis win support?
options: Mass unemployment made desperate voters open to extreme promises
It made Germany wealthy enough to rearm
It cancelled the Treaty of Versailles
It automatically ended the Weimar constitution
questions.answer: Mass unemployment made desperate voters open to extreme promises
questions.why: Six million unemployed by 1932. Desperation makes radical voices sound reasonable — the middle link of the causal chain you already own.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: EXTRACT: "His specs — use them as burning glasses!" The boys grab Piggy's glasses to light the fire. What does this moment show about Piggy's role?
options: His intelligence is useful to the group but exploited — they take from him without respect
He is secretly the strongest leader
He starts the fire to seize power
questions.answer: His intelligence is useful to the group but exploited — they take from him without respect
questions.why: They need what Piggy has, never Piggy himself. Extract questions work exactly like this: small moment, big meaning — the same skill as your upcoming assessment.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: Which of these is a PULL factor for moving to a city?
questions.why: Pull = what draws you IN (jobs ahead of you). The other three all push you OUT of where you are. Same rule as last night, new angle.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A prism's end face has area 12 cm² and the prism is 7 cm long. Volume?
questions.why: Cross-section × length: 12 × 7 = 84. (19 is the adding trap, 42 the phantom halving.) Same formula you answered at speed last night — now applied.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: EXTRACT MODE — same skill as your upcoming assessment. Early in the novel, the boys vote Ralph chief 'with the conch in his hands', even though Jack already leads the choir. In your own words: WHY does holding the conch win Ralph the vote — and what does that tell us about what the boys value at the start? Point → evidence → explain.
